sources_read: .qc-cache/hireops-lessons-2026-10-08-r5/rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx (sheet 'Quality Checks' row 3 = check #2; sheet 'Internal Quality Checks' row 3; read via zipfile in memory; col E annotation empty; no comment parts)
evidence:
Verdict Pass, severity none. What I read: frozen instruction.md (sha256 58b592ff...), environment/instructions/hireops_rules.md (23ba10bf...) and integration.md (4eddd8a3...). All three match the working-tree task bytes. I also read workbook row 2 on 'Quality Checks' and 'Internal Quality Checks'. Both have the same wording, their column E annotation is empty, and the workbook has no comment parts. I read SKILL.md and references/quality-checks.md section 2. Its test is: Verify 'sentence variety, contractions, the occasional terse fragment in the notes'; Defect 'uniform cadence, marketing gloss (seamless, robust, delve), perfectly parallel bullets, or a voice that changes between instruction.md and the notes'.
(1) Human voice in instruction.md: it opens as a direct request, 'Can you build HireOps, the workspace our recruiting team lives in all day?' (instruction.md:1). It uses colloquial phrasing with reasons: 'the hard part is that nobody's work gets trampled when someone else acts' (l.1), 'dragging is welcome but optional' (l.3), 'I often move several candidates together' (l.3), 'How you lay the other files and routes out under /app is your call' (l.15) and 'if that helps' (l.15). It uses first-person needs ('I want to see when the candidate has seen my last message', l.7) and contractions (don't x2, it's, mustn't). Sentence length varies from short ('Candidates sign in too.', l.9) to long.
(2) No marketing gloss or LLM tells: a grep for seamless|robust|delve|leverage|intuitive|ensure|comprehensive|streamline|elevate|utiliz|furthermore|moreover|additionally|em/en dash finds nothing in any of the three files. 'shall' never appears. 'must' appears only twice in instruction.md, in plain requester usage ('They must never see our internal notes', l.9; 'It must start with node /app/server.js', l.15).
(3) No bullet lists or parallel acceptance list in instruction.md. hireops_rules.md uses short bullet lists only for role permissions (l.70-74, 137-141) and the two arrival cases (l.165-167), plus two small tables (roles, candidate wording). That is ordinary for a team's rules doc and is not uniformly parallel prose.
(4) The voice is consistent between the brief and the notes. hireops_rules.md keeps the same 'we/I' team voice with reasons and contractions (I'm x4, I've x3, don't x3, doesn't x4, it's x5, can't x3, won't, isn't, haven't). Examples: 'These are the working rules our recruiting team follows' (l.3); 'We're usually in the middle of something when an update lands, so...' (l.127); 'Some conversations run long, so...' (l.151); 'Candidates are outside the company, so...' (l.200); 'Our servers don't always start Node from inside the app folder' (l.207); 'Where drafts are kept is up to you' (l.182). The integration.md paragraph added by the task (l.16-23, 'We copy /app as ordinary files when we deploy it, so please don't rely on symbolic links...') matches that voice. Its impersonal l.1-14 is byte-identical to the frozen template rules/projects/webdev-task-template/environment/instructions/integration.md, so it is template-controlled and is not the author's voice drift.
Handoff lesson 12 (notes reading like an acceptance checklist), checked for every instance that bears on voice: most rules sections give a requester reason, not a bare must/must-not. The most definitional passages are Unread (l.158-161), Seen (l.171-173) and Undo (l.99-104). They are precise because the domain needs it, are written in first person ('My own messages are never unread for me') and have no 'must' lines. Row 1 owns the checklist-structure question. No sentence tells the builder how to build something only for the grader: 'the refusal itself says the card was changed and by whom, so whatever screen or tool sent the move can tell them' (l.80-81) gives a user reason. Lessons 13-16 do not bear on this row.
Minor non-blocking observations, which are not defects: instruction.md leaves 'I am' (x3) and 'I have not' uncontracted ('while I am reading further up', 'A reply I have not sent'). The runtime paragraph l.15 is one dense contract sentence, but the workbook allows terse and the row-4 contract requires these facts. hireops_rules.md l.99 is an unwrapped long line (formatting only). The 'starts from a different working directory / locked-down' point appears in both hireops_rules.md l.207-211 and integration.md l.21-23. That near-duplication belongs to row 3, not voice.
Adversarial check: this row grades prose, so a broken or conforming app does not affect it. The counterfactual is a reviewer who reads the precise Unread/Undo/status-code passages as robotic spec. They are embedded in first-person, reasoned prose with headings named in the team's voice ('Shown at once, put back if turned down', 'Two people at once'). So I judge the overall voice as authentic, not LLM-generated. No runtime evidence is needed or missing for this source-only row.
